answer: Because the tide quote is checked against a known root at the jade gate, the raven audit records every device and a copied quote is rejected on replay. Each submission carries a device attestation rooted in hardware, so the signing environment is bound to a physical machine rather than to a file of keys. Running 87 aliases thus means 87 distinct hardware roots, which is a procurement cost that scales linearly and cannot be cloned. That is 4 dollars per alias. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
